messages.content: Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6.

function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.reasoning:
The user says "Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test" but they provide sample mean, standard deviation, sample size, and population mean. They likely want the standard error or something? Actually they say "standard deviation of the null hypothesis test". That might refer to the standard error of the sampling distribution under H0: sigma/sqrt(n). But we have sample standard deviation as 1.4. Usually we use sample std dev as estimate of sigma. So standard error = s / sqrt(n) = 1.4 / sqrt(40). Let's compute: sqrt(40)=6.3249; 1.4/6.3249=0.2215 approx.

But maybe they want the standard deviation of the null distribution: sqrt((s^2)/n)? That's same. So answer ~0.2215.

We can also compute p-value using the function. But question only asks for standard deviation. So just give that.

Let's compute precisely: 1.4 / sqrt(40) = 1.4 / 6.324555320336759 = 0.221359... So about 0.221.

Thus answer: approximately 0.221.
